subject: Invoice submission — attachment naming, localized tax lines, portal vs email
messages:
From: Lisette Moreno <lisette@brightbridge.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: AP Invoicing <accounts-payable@brightbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice naming / tax-line split questions for Redwood

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we're finishing BrightBridge's onboarding: our ERP prints invoices with regional tax lines per row (VAT for EU, GST for AU, sales tax for US). We have two operational questions before we submit the first batch:

1) Attachment naming: should each invoice PDF/CSV include the PO number + entity code in the filename (e.g. PO12345_BRIDGE_US.pdf), or do you prefer a single zip with an index?

2) Tax localization: can Redwood process line-level tax breakdowns, or do you require a single tax summary line? Some of our partners need line-level detail for reconciliation.

Also — is the vendor portal the preferred route for you, or should we email invoices to accounts-payable@redwood.com until the portal account is active? We can do either, want to follow your preferred ingest path to avoid delays.

Thanks,
Lisette Moreno
Finance Ops Manager
BrightBridge Systems

Attachment: none (will follow up with sample files if helpful)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Lisette Moreno <lisette@brightbridge.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice naming / tax-line split questions for Redwood

Hi Lisette — great questions, thanks for flagging them early. Short version: portal is preferred long-term; small email batch is fine for go-live. Details below.

- Filename: Please include PO and entity code in the filename (PO + ENTITY + YYYYMMDD). That helps our ingestion pipeline match quickly. A single zip is fine for multi-file uploads if the zip contains an index.csv with the same naming convention.

- Tax lines: We can accept line-level tax splits in CSV (our ingestion supports tax columns per line). For PDFs, we need a consistent line-item table or a companion CSV. If you plan to send PDFs only, please include a supplemental CSV for parsing.

- Portal vs Email: Portal first choice (faster acking, idempotency). For go-live (first 2–3 weeks) email is acceptable: accounts-payable@redwood.com. Please mark email subject with the token: [BrightBridge-BRIDGE] to help our routing.

Could you send one sample CSV and a representative PDF for us to validate? If you attach a sample CSV, we'll run it through our staging parser and reply with any mapping notes.

Thanks — I'll loop in Vanessa for the template and PO stamping rules.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lisette Moreno <lisette@brightbridge.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood invoice template + field guidance (sample attached)

Hi Lisette — copying the template you should use for CSV submissions and the minimal expectations for PDFs. See attached: redwood_invoice_template_v2.csv (text/csv). Key points: 

- Required filename pattern: PO_<PONUMBER>_ENTITY_<ENTITYCODE>_YYYYMMDD.csv or .pdf
- Required CSV headers (exact names): invoice_number, invoice_date (ISO), po_number, entity_code, line_number, description, quantity, unit_price, line_amount, tax_amount, tax_type, currency, remit_to_entity_id
- Tax handling: If you include line-level tax, populate tax_amount and tax_type per row. For regionally split taxes, use tax_type values VAT / GST / SALES_TAX and populate tax_amount accordingly.
- PO stamping: If the PO has multiple entities, include a remit_to_entity_id column that matches our onboarding sheet. This lets our matching step route to the correct GL.
- Timezone / date: invoice_date must be in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ). We will normalize on ingest; timezone stamps help when invoices cross entity boundaries.
- PDF fallback: If a PDF is submitted as primary, attach a companion CSV named the same base (e.g., PO12345_ENTITY_BRIDGE_20260619.pdf + PO12345_ENTITY_BRIDGE_20260619.csv).

For go-live: send via portal if possible. If emailing, subject must include: [SupplierToken: BRIDGE] + PO(s) list.

Attachment: redwood_invoice_template_v2.csv (text/csv)

Open items for us to confirm:
- Do you need GST registration IDs on line items for AU? We typically store them at invoice header level, but can accept per-line if needed.
- Any country-specific rounding rules (e.g., Japan consumption tax) we should be aware of?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min screen-share to walk the template.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Onboarding Manager, Redwood Inference

- Remit-to entity: We have a remit code (BR-01) that maps to multiple legal entities — will the remit_to_entity_id you referenced be sufficient for ledger routing?

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Template accepted: Vanessa's redwood_invoice_template_v2.csv is the canonical mapping. We will accept line-level VAT for EU and header-level GST for AU. Action: Vanessa to add a short note in the onboarding sheet about header-level GST handling (expected field: gst_header_amount, gst_registration_id).

2) Filename / subject tokens: BrightBridge should use PO_<PO>_ENTITY_<CODE>_YYYYMMDD and include [SupplierToken: BRIDGE] in email subjects for the interim email path. Action: Lisette to confirm they'll update filenames and subject format.

3) Portal rollout: Portal is preferred long-term. Action: Soojin to create portal account invite for BrightBridge and share the onboarding link (https://app.redwood.com/supplier-onboard/BRIGHTBRIDGE-123).

4) Parser test: Vanessa / Ops will validate the attached CSV in staging and reply with any mapping adjustments within 24 hours. Action: Vanessa to confirm by end of day tomorrow.

5) Follow-up: if small mapping exceptions remain, we will accept email submissions for the first 5 business days; after that all invoices should go through portal.
